context: Observed bounded Continuum Rust/rusqlite WAL experiment. Every CLI command currently calls Store::open: Connection::open, busy_timeout5sec, foreign_keysON, synchronousFULL, BEGIN IMMEDIATE to inspect appid/schema and initialize only emptydb, commit, ensure WAL (possibly PRAGMAjournalmode). Existing-only CLI guard checks file exists except init/demo. Under another connection holding BEGINIMMEDIATE with NO data changes, native get/head/receipt each waited ~5.011sec then returned exit1, empty stdout, database error: database is locked. Same-build native SQLite3.53.2 read-only connection (SQLITE_OPEN_READ_ONLY) returned committed head and exact receipt plus object canonical-byte length with the reservation held. Baseline/postrollback get/head/receipt stdout equal; originalevent/head unchanged. Native writer code unchanged. Experiment only demonstrates this controlled contention; no throughput benchmark. Need preserve appid/schema rejection, exact object validation and acceptance semantics. Current CLI pure reads: get,head,receipt,events,inspect-context,verify-context,verify-current-context,verify-handoff. prepare-context/acknowledge-handoff create objects; accept/blob/put/init/demo mutate. backup reads source but writes a separate file. Existing Store::open must retain safe initialization and WAL+FULL for writers. No read-only native Store path implemented yet.
request: In <=250 words, judge the smallest safe next implementation boundary for this observed issue. Identify concrete tests that would falsify the change and one important failure mode. Should a separate existing-only read-only Store open route pure read CLI commands while leaving writable initialization unchanged? Do not broaden into a replacement database or claim the probe proved a production performance gain.
